summary: Signed-in user menu for the header: avatar (with fallback initials), name, email and role, customizable items, and a separate “Esci” (Sign out) item.
whenToUse: In the actions area of Header, SiteHeader, or AppShell when the user is signed in.
whenNotToUse: For signed-out users: show an “Accedi” (Sign in) Button or Link.
As the portal's main navigation: use Sidebar or NavigationMenu.

props.name: user
props.description: Identity shown in the trigger and in the block at the top of the menu.

props.name: onAction
props.description: Called for items without href. Items with href navigate (RouterProvider).

props.name: onSignOut
props.description: When provided, adds an “Esci” (Sign out) item at the bottom, after a separator. It does not perform any sign-out: the consumer does.

props.name: showName
props.description: Visibility of the name next to the avatar; “wide” shows it from 768 px.

props.name: placement
props.description: Menu position relative to the trigger.

inherits: Items are DropdownMenu MenuItems, with all their props (href, isDisabled, tone, shortcut…).

keyboard.action: Opens the menu and moves focus to the first item.
Activates the item and closes the menu.
Closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger.

accessibility: The trigger is a <button> named “Menu account, {nome}” with aria-haspopup/aria-expanded.
The menu takes its name from the trigger; the identity block (email, role) is linked with aria-describedby but is not a menu item, so it does not interfere with keyboard navigation.
The avatar is decorative: the name is always available as accessible text.
Built on react-aria-components (APG Menu Button pattern).
responsive: Below 768 px (showName="wide") only the avatar remains visible; the full name is in the menu.
The panel never exceeds the viewport width; long names and emails wrap instead of being cut off.
customization: Use MenuSection with title for groups (e.g. “Organization”).
Use USER_MENU_SIGN_OUT_KEY if you handle all actions in onAction and need to detect sign-out.
commonMistakes: Signing out only on the client: always invalidate the session on the server.
Putting critical information (e.g. password expiration) only in the menu: also show it on the page.

examples.name: LoggedUserHeader
examples.title: Header with a signed-in user
examples.description: Items show the chosen action; “Esci” replaces the menu with the “Accedi” button (local state).

examples.name: AlwaysShowName
examples.title: Always-visible name and English labels
examples.description: Long name and email, custom sign-out text.

limits: Account/organization switching must be composed by the consumer with MenuSection and MenuItem.
